title: Pune Road Trip
description: A scenic road trip through the Western Ghats, filled with lush valleys, historic forts, and local flavours.
story:
We set off early on a Saturday morning with the monsoon clouds already gathering over the hills. The drive through the Ghats was breathtaking — every hairpin bend revealed a new curtain of green.

We stopped at Sinhagad Fort just as the morning mist was lifting, and the view across the valley was worth every step of the climb. A local family shared their packed breakfast with us at the summit, and we sat there for longer than we planned, watching the clouds move through the valleys below.

The rest of the day was a blur of roadside vada pav, spontaneous detours, and the kind of conversations you only have when you're far from home. By the time we rolled back into the city, sunburned and grinning, we were already planning the next one.

title: Goa December Getaway
description: Sun, sea, and spice — a long-overdue trip to Goa during the festive season.
story:
December in Goa is everything the postcards promise and a little more. The beaches were quieter in the mornings, before the crowds arrived, and we made a habit of catching sunrise with coffee from a shack already busy with fishermen.

The Portuguese architecture of Old Goa was stunning — those white basilicas glowing in the afternoon heat. We ended each evening at a different beach shack, eating prawn curry and listening to live music. The spice plantation tour was a highlight neither of us expected: walking through rows of vanilla, cardamom, and nutmeg, learning how so much of what we cook every day starts here.

It was exactly the reset we needed.

title: Kedarnath Yatra
description: A seven-day pilgrimage and trek to one of the holiest Himalayan shrines — Kedarnath temple at 3,583 m.

videos.title: Trek to Kedarnath — afternoon on the trail

story:
The train to Haridwar was packed with pilgrims, all bound for the same sacred hills. We arrived at dawn and the station was already alive — vendors, sadhus, families with children, everyone moving in the same direction.

The drive to Gaurikund the next day wound through cedar forests and narrow gorges, the road hugging the Mandakini all the way up. The base camp at Gaurikund smelled of wood smoke and chai, and we slept early, knowing the real climb started at sunrise.

The 16-km trek to Kedarnath took everything we had. The trail switches between stone steps, mountain streams, and sheer rocky faces. We overtook mule trains and were overtaken by older pilgrims who seemed to float upward. By the time the temple came into view — that ancient stone tower rising against the white peaks — the exhaustion vanished.

The two days at Kedarnath were unlike anything else. The air is so thin and clear that the mountains feel close enough to touch. We woke before dawn on the last morning to walk the glacier path, and watched the sunrise set the peaks on fire one by one.

Coming down was its own kind of pilgrimage.

title: Chikkamagalur
description: Misty hills, coffee estates, and forest trails through the Western Ghats.
story:
The drive into Chikkamagalur winds through endless rows of coffee and cardamom, the air thick with fragrance. Mornings here start before sunrise — mist rolling down the hills, the only sounds being birdsong and the distant hum of a tractor on the estate.

We trekked up to Mullayanagiri, the highest peak in Karnataka, and stood above the clouds for a good half hour before they swallowed the view again. Hebbe Falls was the other highlight — a two-hour hike through dense forest to reach a waterfall that drops nearly 170 feet into a rock pool.

The evenings were slow and cold, spent by a bonfire with a mug of the freshest filter coffee we had ever tasted.

title: Mysore
description: The city of palaces — royal grandeur, sandalwood, and silk in the cultural heart of Karnataka.
story:
Mysore moves at a gentler pace than most Indian cities, and that is exactly what we needed. The palace was the obvious first stop — we arrived early to beat the crowds and had the marble corridors almost to ourselves, sunlight slanting through the stained-glass ceiling and lighting up the floor in patches of colour.

Chamundi Hills at dawn was worth the early alarm: the city spread below in a haze of gold, the temple bells just starting. We spent an afternoon wandering Devaraja Market, buying sandalwood soap and bags of jasmine that filled the car all the way home.

Mysore reminded us that not every trip needs to be an adventure. Sometimes slow and beautiful is enough.

title: Pondicherry
description: French boulevards, Tamil temples, and the quiet rhythm of a coastal town unlike anywhere else in India.
story:
Pondicherry feels like two cities sharing one shoreline. On one side the French Quarter, all yellow walls and bougainvillea tumbling over wrought-iron balconies. On the other, the Tamil Quarter — dense, loud, colourful, and very much alive.

We spent our first morning cycling through the French streets before the heat set in, stopping at a bakery that served proper croissants and strong coffee. Auroville was a strange and peaceful detour — the Matrimandir at its centre, a golden sphere in the middle of a forest, still under some kind of permanent contemplation.

The evenings on the Promenade were the best part: the sea breeze, street food vendors, families out for their evening walk, and the old lighthouse blinking steadily over it all.
